summary: Total Field was designed to help anyone understand how their surrounding soil is changing and how to protect its health. Focusing primarily on agricultural workers, we prioritized an intuitive user interface that translates vast, complex NASA datasets into clear, actionable insights. While raw satellite data can be overwhelming to navigate, it is essential for the daily decisions that directly impact farmers' livelihoods—and Total Field bridges that gap.
details:
OverviewTotal Field (demonstrated in our interactive platform, Field Shift) is a web-based agricultural decision-support tool designed to help farmers and land workers understand how their soil is changing and protect its long-term health. While NASA Earth observation datasets provide vital environmental intelligence, their scale and technical complexity make them difficult for everyday growers to navigate. Total Field bridges this gap through a simple, 3-step guided workflow that translates complex satellite and soil data into clear, actionable 3-year crop rotation strategies.

How It Works: A 3-Step Guided Workflow

  • Step 1 — My Field (Geolocation & Plot Selection): Users locate their farm effortlessly by searching a town or city, using their device's GPS, entering latitude/longitude coordinates, tapping directly on an interactive Leaflet map, or exploring pre-loaded sample farms.
  • Step 2 — Field Conditions (Automated Environmental & Soil Diagnostics): The platform evaluates localized weather, rainfall, and soil conditions to flag critical risk indicators—such as heat stress combined with low surface soil moisture, extended bare-soil periods, and repeated consecutive crops. Users can also inspect 10-year historical crop records alongside USDA soil (SSURGO) and crop mapping layers.
  • Step 3 — My Options (28-Rule Fuzzy Model & 3-Year Crop Rotation Planner): Farmers select their top operational priority—Save Water, Protect Soil Health, Increase Earnings, or Reduce Erosion—along with their current/previous crop, planned planting date, and optional local soil organic matter percentage. Running our 28-rule CosoNASA fuzzy model (powered by 2015–2024 NASA POWER monthly climatology and NASA SMAP soil moisture data), the system generates tailored 3-year crop rotation plans (such as Safflower → Winter Wheat → Cover Crop for water resilience), estimating water usage differences (mm/cycle) and gross revenue impacts.

Advanced Tools & Practical Portability

  • Scenario Comparison & Sensitivity Simulator: Growers and researchers can compare three possible future scenarios side by side, adjust assumptions in a sensitivity simulator, check published USDA market prices, and inspect transparent data-source statuses.
  • Offline-Ready Field Reports: Users can copy a plain-text summary, export scenario data as a CSV, or download a complete English PDF field assessment containing their field diagnostics, scenario limits, and a practical field-check checklist to take directly into the field.
